title: Define accessible accent harmonies and fluid spacing system
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Refresh the design token set to introduce a small palette of accessible accent harmonies, a fluid typography scale using clamp(), and a reworked spacing/radius system that scales across breakpoints. The goal is to improve legibility, ensure WCAG AA (and where reasonable AAA) contrast for primary interactive states, simplify migration for components, and reduce bespoke spacing hacks across the component library.
acceptance_criteria: New accent palette defined with 6 semantic tokens (accent-strong, accent, accent-muted, accent-foreground, accent-outline, accent-hover) with documented contrast ratios >= 4.5:1 against background for body text and 3:1 for larger text where appropriate.
Fluid type scale implemented with CSS token examples using clamp() for h1..body-sm and token names published in Figma and code spec.

Spacing system replaced by a 4-step modular scale (xs, sm, md, lg) plus extended gutters with explicit pixel fallbacks; radius tokens normalized to a 3-tier system (radius-none, radius-base, radius-pill).
Dark mode variants provided for all color tokens with parity tests passing (visual snapshots) and automated contrast checks in CI.
Migration guide created mapping old tokens to new tokens and a staged rollout plan for components: buttons, forms, tables, and charts.
Design review sign-off from two product designers and one accessibility reviewer; engineering feasibility sign-off from frontend lead.
rollout_notes: Phase 1: publish token package behind feature flag and update internal storybook components. Phase 2: apply to buttons and primary form inputs in canary release (5% traffic). Phase 3: charts and tables; monitor metrics (visual-regressions, token-usage, and CTR for CTA variants). Full release coordinated with runtime-1.18 release window.
decisions: Use semantic token names (accent-*, spacing-*) rather than color/value names to reduce coupling to implementation details.
Prioritize contrast over pure vibrancy for primary interactive states; use subtle saturation boosts for hover/active to maintain perceived liveliness.
Implement fluid typography with clamp() and provide static fallbacks for IE/legacy builds via tokenized media queries.
Limit radius options to three tiers to reduce cognitive load for component authors and simplify composability.
open_questions: Do we standardize accent-foreground on accent-strong or allow per-component overrides for iconography?
Should charts receive a separate harmonized palette (data-driven colors) or consume the same semantic accents with adapted saturation?
What is the acceptable performance budget for runtime theme switching in V2 of the Console (frame-rate and reflow concerns)?
